summary: Describes an architecture for SNMP management frameworks, designed to be modular so SNMP standards can evolve over time. This was the first SNMPv3 architecture document and was replaced by RFC 2271.

eli5.summary: It is the blueprint that shows all the parts of a network management system and how they fit, so each part can be upgraded separately.

questions: how are snmp management frameworks described
what are the snmpv3 security levels
subtitle: The vocabulary and building blocks that let SNMP management frameworks evolve piece by piece.

tldr.problem: SNMP lacked secure SET support, which the RFC calls the most important deficiency in SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c, and its standards were hard to evolve one piece at a time.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2261 defines a modular architecture. An SNMP entity is an engine (dispatcher, message processing, security and access control subsystems) plus applications, with abstract service interfaces between the parts.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2261 was the first SNMPv3 architecture document and has been obsoleted by RFC 2271.

today: RFC 2261 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 2271, so it describes an early version of the SNMPv3 architecture.

sections.title: Goals and Scope
sections.content:
This document defines a vocabulary for describing SNMP Management Frameworks and an architecture for their major portions. It is not a general introduction to SNMP and does not give its history.

The goals include using existing material (it is heavily based on the work informally known as SNMPv2u and SNMPv2*), addressing the need for secure SET support, keeping SNMP as simple as possible, making a minimal conforming implementation inexpensive, and allowing portions of SNMP to be upgraded without disrupting an entire framework. It is meant to fit minimal agents, proxy agents, command line managers, dual-role entities and large management stations.
sections.eli5: The aim is a system where you can replace one part, like the lock on a door, without rebuilding the whole house.

sections.title: Design Decisions and Document Set
sections.content:
The architecture draws conceptual boundaries between documents. Each piece, with its elements of procedure and the MIB objects it needs, should be defined in a self-contained document, so security models, authentication and privacy mechanisms and message formats can be upgraded and can move along the standards track on different time-lines. Security and access control add many configuration parameters and frequent changes of secrets, so these must be remotely configurable. The design also tries to keep simple devices cheap while letting complex environments extend the simple one.

The document set covers transport mappings, message processing, security, access control, protocol operations, applications, structure of management information, textual conventions, conformance statements and MIB modules. A subsystem is an abstract, incomplete specification of a portion of a framework. A model is a specific design of a subsystem, detailed enough to implement.
sections.eli5: The rulebook is split into small booklets, one per job. Each booklet can be rewritten on its own schedule.

sections.title: SNMP Entities, Engines and Applications
sections.content:
An SNMP entity is an implementation of the architecture: one SNMP engine plus one or more applications. The engine is identified by an snmpEngineID and contains four parts.

  • A Dispatcher, one per engine, which sends and receives messages, picks the right Message Processing Model by version, and gives applications an abstract way to send and receive PDUs.
  • A Message Processing Subsystem, holding one or more models, such as SNMPv3, SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c, each defining one message format.
  • A Security Subsystem, offering authentication and privacy through one or more Security Models, such as the User-Based Security Model.
  • An Access Control Subsystem, offering authorization through one or more Access Control Models, such as the View-Based Access Control Model.

Applications use the engine's services. They include command generators, command responders, notification originators, notification receivers and proxy forwarders. An entity with command generators or notification receivers has traditionally been called a manager, and one with command responders or notification originators an agent.
sections.eli5: Think of a post office with a front desk, a form-filler, a security guard and a rule-keeper. The people who send and read mail are the applications that use the post office.

sections.title: Naming Identities and Management Information
sections.content:
A principal is the who on whose behalf processing takes place. A securityName is a human-readable string for a principal, usable outside any one Security Model. Each Security Model maps it to and from its own model-dependent security ID, such as a community name or user name.

Management information lives in contexts. A context is a collection of management information accessible by an SNMP entity, and is always a subset of a single entity. It is named by a contextEngineID and a contextName, and each contextName MUST be unique within an entity. A scopedPDU carries a contextEngineID, a contextName and a PDU.

Every message has a securityLevel, one of three ordered values: noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv and authPriv.
sections.eli5: A principal is who is asking, and a context is which cupboard of information they want to look in. Each message also says how secret it must be: not at all, signed, or signed and locked.

sections.title: Abstract Service Interfaces
sections.content:
The subsystems talk to each other through abstract primitives. These are not code interfaces, only a description of the services and the data passed. The Dispatcher offers sendPdu, processPdu, returnResponsePdu and processResponsePdu, plus registerContextEngineID so an application can claim responsibility for certain PDU types. The Message Processing Subsystem offers prepareOutgoingMessage, prepareResponseMessage and prepareDataElements. The Security Subsystem offers generateRequestMsg, processIncomingMsg and generateResponseMsg. The Access Control Subsystem offers isAccessAllowed.

The RFC shows two scenarios, one for a command generator and one for a command responder. The request path runs from the application through the Dispatcher and the message processing model to the security model, and the response comes back through the same layers.

Section 5 also defines the SNMP-FRAMEWORK-MIB, which instruments the engine with objects such as snmpEngineID, snmpEngineBoots, snmpEngineTime and snmpEngineMaxMessageSize.
sections.eli5: Each part passes a message down the line, and each adds its own step, like an assembly line. The answer comes back along the same line.

sections.title: Threats and Security Responsibilities
sections.content:
A Security Model SHOULD protect against four principal threats: modification of information, masquerade, message stream modification (malicious re-ordering, delay or replay) and disclosure. It need not protect against denial of service or traffic analysis. The RFC reasons that denial-of-service attacks are often indistinguishable from ordinary network failures, and that management traffic patterns are predictable.

The level of security actually provided depends on the Security and Access Control Models used. Applications have access to data that is not secured and should take reasonable steps to protect it from disclosure. The purchaser of an implementation is responsible for checking that it follows the architecture, that the models meet the organization's needs, that models and applications follow their specifications, and that configuration secrets are protected from inadvertent disclosure.
sections.eli5: The design protects against people changing, faking, replaying or spying on messages. It does not try to stop someone from just flooding the line.
